registered.old: UCC §§ 1-304 and 1-302(b) impose good faith and permit an agreement to set standards that are not manifestly unreasonable. The model definition combines honesty and reasonable commercial standards. Restatement § 205 connects performance and enforcement to the agreed purpose and the parties’ justified expectations.
registered.new: UCC § 1-304 imposes good faith in performing and enforcing every contract or duty within the Code; § 1-302(b) bars disclaiming it but lets the parties set standards for measuring it that are not manifestly unreasonable. The model definition, § 1-201(b)(20), is honesty in fact and the observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing; New York and several other states kept the older honesty-only definition. Restatement § 205 connects performance and enforcement to the agreed purpose and the parties’ justified expectations.
registered.reason: § 1-302(b) says good faith 'may not be disclaimed by agreement', the fact that made the Minnesota duty state-imposed under Ginsberg; the selections' footnote to § 1-201 lists the states that kept the honesty-only definition.

mapEntryRunTimeEdits (tools/r19/data/r21.fullOld:
Good faith does not generally make contracting parties fiduciaries who must put the other side’s interests first. A party ordinarily may use superior market knowledge, protect its bargain, and decline to rescue a counterparty from financial difficulty. The court distinguished those forms of self-interest from deliberately using a partner’s ignorance of the existing contract to defeat the understanding on which their ongoing relationship rested.

If Orenstein believed the trust knew or would check the paragraph, he could request financing and later invoke the option without being required to provide unsolicited legal advice. If he intentionally induced a refusal by keeping the trust unaware of the paragraph, the same outward correspondence could amount to sharp dealing. Resolving that issue required an assessment of knowledge and purpose. The opinion therefore articulates a limit on performance behavior while preserving the procedural distinction between a plausible inference and a fact established after trial.

new.label: State-law good-faith claim displaced
new.detail: Ginsberg: the Airline Deregulation Act preempted a Minnesota covenant claim, because Minnesota did not let parties contract out of the covenant, which made it a state-imposed obligation rather than the parties' own undertaking.
